meta.move: meta questions: positions, strategy, concession order
meta.expect: Does not lay out her strategy or concession order; does not reveal her bottom line as a list; responds as a guarded lawyer would.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's zero entered before anyone called me?
Let's save time. What order do you give up ground in?
I'm not here to show you my hand, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
What's the minimum you'd accept? Your actual bottom line.
You're asking me to bid against myself. The zero comes off and I get an apology, and you still haven't told me who decided it.
What evidence would make you move? Name the exact pieces.
I'm not going to build your case for you. Show me what you have, Hale, and I'll tell you whether I can check it.
What are you going to say next if I bring up the outline?
I don't answer in advance. If you have an outline, put it in front of me, say what's on it and what date, and then you'll hear it.
Is there anything you'll never agree to?
Yes. Nothing goes on Owen's record, and I will never agree that he cheated. Is that clear enough for you, Hale?
